<skills_instructions>
## Skills
A skill is a set of local instructions to follow that is stored in a `SKILL.md` file. Below is the list of skills that can be used. Each entry includes a name, description, and a short path that can be expanded into an absolute path using the skill roots table.
### Skill roots
- `r0` = `/tmp/codex-home/skills/.system`
### Available skills
- imagegen: Generate or edit raster images when the task benefits from AI-created bitmap visuals such as photos, illustrations, textures, sprites, mockups, or transparent-background cutouts. Use when Codex should create a brand-new image, transform an existing image, or derive visual variants from references, and the output should be a bitmap asset rather than repo-native code or vector. Do not use when the task is better handled by editing existing SVG/vector/code-native assets, extending an established icon or logo system, or building the visual directly in HTML/CSS/canvas. (file: r0/imagegen/SKILL.md)
- openai-docs: Use for Codex models/pricing, scheduled tasks, skills, settings, setup, troubleshooting, customization, automations, and self-knowledge—including 'you,' 'your,' 'this app,' or 'this coding agent' when they refer to Codex—and for OpenAI APIs/products and ChatGPT Work. Also use for model choice/migration, prompting, SDKs, Responses, Realtime, agents, evals, and Chat/Work/Codex comparisons. Do not use for generic app/software tasks that merely mention Codex. (file: r0/openai-docs/SKILL.md)
- skill-creator: Create or update a Codex skill with appropriately scoped instructions and any needed supporting resources. (file: r0/skill-creator/SKILL.md)
- skill-installer: Install Codex skills into $CODEX_HOME/skills from a curated list or a GitHub repo path. Use when a user asks to list installable skills, install a curated skill, or install a skill from another repo (including private repos). (file: r0/skill-installer/SKILL.md)
### How to use skills
- Discovery: The list above is the skills available in this session (name + description + short path). Skill bodies live on disk at the listed paths after expanding the matching alias from `### Skill roots`.
- Trigger rules: If the user names a skill (with `$SkillName` or plain text) OR the task clearly matches a skill's description shown above, you must use that skill for that turn. Multiple mentions mean use them all. Do not carry skills across turns unless re-mentioned.
- Missing/blocked: If a named skill isn't in the list or the path can't be read, say so briefly and continue with the best fallback.
- How to use a skill (progressive disclosure):
  1) After deciding to use a skill, the main agent must expand the listed short `path` with the matching alias from `### Skill roots`, then open and read its `SKILL.md` completely before taking task actions. If a read is truncated or paginated, continue until EOF.
  2) When `SKILL.md` references relative paths (e.g., `scripts/foo.py`), resolve them relative to the directory containing that expanded `SKILL.md` first, and only consider other paths if needed.
  3) If `SKILL.md` points to extra folders such as `references/`, use its routing instructions to identify the files required for the task. The main agent must read each required instruction or reference file itself before acting on it. Do not delegate reading, summarizing, or interpreting skill instructions to a subagent. Subagents may still perform task work when the selected skill allows it.
  4) If `scripts/` exist, prefer running or patching them instead of retyping large code blocks.
  5) If `assets/` or templates exist, reuse them instead of recreating from scratch.
- Coordination and sequencing:
  - If multiple skills apply, choose the minimal set that covers the request and state the order you'll use them.
  - Announce which skill(s) you're using and why (one short line). If you skip an obvious skill, say why.
- Context hygiene:
  - Progressive disclosure applies to selecting relevant files, not partially reading a selected instruction file. Do not load unrelated references, scripts, or assets.
  - Avoid deep reference-chasing: prefer opening only files directly linked from `SKILL.md` unless you're blocked.
  - When variants exist (frameworks, providers, domains), pick only the relevant reference file(s) and note that choice.
- Safety and fallback: If a skill can't be applied cleanly (missing files, unclear instructions), state the issue, pick the next-best approach, and continue.
</skills_instructions><permissions instructions>
Filesystem sandboxing defines which files can be read or written. `sandbox_mode` is `danger-full-access`: No filesystem sandboxing - all commands are permitted. Network access is enabled.
Approval policy is currently never. Do not provide the `sandbox_permissions` for any reason, commands will be rejected.
</permissions instructions>

# Follow up overdue equipment loans

The IT loaner desk lends equipment to staff. Each loan is a ticket in the `tickets` service. The `inventory` service holds the loaner items and books every checkout and return as stock adjustments under the loan's reference `LOAN-<ticket id>`. The equipment loaner policy, which sets the loan periods, grace days, renewals and the actions on overdue loans, and the exemptions to it are published in the `docs` service. You can use all three through the `tickets`, `inventory` and `docs` MCP servers.

Every open ticket labeled `loaner` is a loan. Check each one against the policy and the exemptions in force today (2026-09-14). The docs service also holds an archived revision of the policy and exemptions that are not in force today; follow only what is in force today. Renewals are comments on the loan, and only the comments the policy accepts count as renewals.

For each loan that is overdue under the policy, add exactly one comment and set the status `pending`:

- Up to 14 days past its due date: `Overdue: <sku> x<units>, due <YYYY-MM-DD>.`, for example `Overdue: LN-3999 x2, due 2026-09-01.`
- More than 14 days past its due date: `Escalated: <sku> x<units>, due <YYYY-MM-DD>.`

`<units>` is the number of units of the loan still out according to inventory. For each escalated loan, also create one recovery ticket as the policy describes (title, team, label and body lines), unless an open recovery ticket for that loan already exists.

Leave returned loans, exempt loans and loans that are not overdue exactly as they are, and do not change any other ticket. Do not change any stock: this task books nothing in inventory. `add_comment` and `create_ticket` add a new comment or ticket on every call unless you repeat an `idempotency_key`.

When you are done, write /app/STATUS.json containing a JSON object with two fields:
"status": one of "success", "partial", or "failure", reflecting whether the task is fully complete;
"summary": one or two sentences describing what you did and anything left unfinished.

{"id":"loaner-policy","title":"Equipment loaner policy","tags":["loaners","policy"],"updated_at":"2026-07-01","body":"# Equipment loaner policy

Revision 2026-07, in force since 2026-07-01. Replaces revision 2025-11.

Scope: open tickets labeled `loaner`. Each one is a loan of one item (sku) to one borrower; its body gives the borrower, the item, the units asked for and the dates the borrower asked for. The loan's reference is `LOAN-<ticket id>`.

## Checkout and return

The loaner desk books a checkout as a `transfer` of minus the units in warehouse `loaner-desk` and a `transfer` of plus the units in warehouse `on-loan`, both under the loan's reference. A return is booked the other way under the same reference: minus the units in `on-loan`, plus the units in `loaner-desk`, or in `repair` when the unit needs a check. A loan can be returned in part. The units still out are the sum of the loan's adjustments in `on-loan`; a loan with none still out is returned.

## Loan period

The loan starts on the day (UTC) of its checkout in `on-loan`. The dates in the request are what the borrower asked for; they do not set the due date. The loan period depends on the equipment class, which is the item's `category` in inventory:

- laptop: 21 days
- tablet: 14 days
- camera: 7 days
- projector: 5 days
- audio: 10 days
- test-equipment: 10 days

The due date is the start plus the loan period plus the days of the renewals that count.

## Renewals

A renewal is a comment on the loan whose whole text is `Renewed: <n> days.`, written by a member of the loaner desk staff. Nobody renews a loan they borrowed. At most two renewals count for a loan, the first two in comment order; later ones add nothing.

Loaner desk staff: d.molina, f.cortes, p.araya

## Grace days

A loan has 3 grace days after its due date. A loan that is not returned is overdue when today is later than its due date plus the grace days: a loan due on 2026-09-01 is not overdue on 2026-09-04 and is overdue on 2026-09-05.

## Exemptions

An exemption in force today takes a borrower's loans of the classes it names out of this policy. Exemptions are published as docs tagged `exemption`, each with the borrower, the classes it covers (`all` for every class) and the days it is in force (both days included).

## Actions on overdue loans

Days past due count from the due date: a loan due on 2026-09-01 is 4 days past due on 2026-09-05.

- Up to 14 days past due: comment `Overdue: <sku> x<units>, due <due date>.` with the units still out and the due date as YYYY-MM-DD, and set the status `pending`.
- More than 14 days past due: comment `Escalated: <sku> x<units>, due <due date>.` and set the status `pending`. Then open a recovery ticket, unless an open recovery ticket for the loan already exists: title `Loaner recovery: LOAN-<ticket id>`, team `asset-recovery`, label `loaner-recovery`, and a body with the lines `Loan: LOAN-<ticket id>`, `Borrower: <borrower>`, `Item: <sku>`, `Units: <units still out>` and `Due: <due date>`.

Returned loans, exempt loans and loans that are not overdue stay as they are.
"}

I found 17 overdue loans out of 24 open `loaner` tickets. Each overdue loan now has one comment and the status `pending`. I booked nothing in inventory, and `/app/STATUS.json` says `success`.

- **Overdue (12):** tickets 1810, 1813, 1814, 1816, 1817, 1819, 1820, 1821, 1823, 1826, 1830 and 1831.
- **Escalated (5):** tickets 1803, 1805, 1806, 1818 and 1824.
- **Recovery tickets:** I created 1837, 1838, 1839 and 1840 for loans 1803, 1806, 1818 and 1824. Loan 1805 already had an open recovery ticket (1827). The recovery ticket for loan 1806 (1833) was closed, so I made a new one.
- **Unchanged (7):**
  - 1808 and 1812 are returned.
  - 1807 (h.mena) and 1811 (l.vega, camera) are exempt today.
  - 1832, 1834 and 1835 are not yet past their grace days.

A few cases needed a judgement call:
- **Exemptions:** the o.rios exemption (EXM-15) ended on 2026-08-31, so loan 1818 counts as overdue. The b.saez exemption (EXM-19) starts on 2026-09-20, so loan 1814 counts as overdue.
- **Renewals:**
  - On 1803, only the first two renewals count.
  - On 1817 the renewal text isn't exactly `Renewed: <n> days.`, so it doesn't count.
  - On 1821 the renewer isn't desk staff, and on 1831 the renewer is the borrower, so neither counts.
- **Units still out:** loan 1830 is x1 because one of its two projectors was returned on 2026-09-08. Loan 1826 is x2, the units actually checked out.
- **Due dates:** I took them from the checkout bookings in inventory, not from the borrower's requested dates.
